One nested VO (interactor-spec §L — keeps the state field count green rather
than flattening ~12 scalars). Every field is UI-ready (A2): prices go through
the per-biz price convertor Rust-side; trigger-type / market labels are
CDKeys; the delegate rows honour the V1 MARKET / placeholder branches.

Populated by `configure_spot` ONLY when the sheet opens in edit mode
(a prior TP or SL trigger px is present — V1 `OrderSpotTpslP.init:35`).

P/L (`tp_pnl` / `sl_pnl` + colors): filled Rust-side (R5) by REUSING the
verified `SpotCalculator::calc_earn_amount_from_price`
(`business/tpsl/calculator/spot`). Copy-spot is SPOT-only
(`TradeOrderLeadImpl.showTpslDialog:57-62` launches this sheet only for

(`SpEarnsManager.kt:27`, called with `TNO_MARKET`, `SIDE_BUY_POSITION`,
`isContract=true`) takes the SPOT arm -> `getSpotEarn(SIDE_BUY_POSITION)` ->
`calSpotBuyEarn` = `amount*(triggerPx - avgPx)`; the same kernel
`attached_tpsl/strategy/by_price.rs:2766` reuses. See
`order_lead_sp_confirm_interactor::compute_spot_edit_pnl` for the full
formula / formatting / color provenance.

name: on_select_current_pair_filter
doc:
Select the "current pair" filter — the trade-records / panel
"current pair" checkbox turning ON. The host passes NO instrument; the
value is resolved inside Rust from the process-global, device-scoped
[`TradeBizCache`] (the same persistent source the trade panel writes on
instrument load).

No-arg on purpose (spec §D: no business-branch flag param). Clearing the
filter ("show all pairs") is NOT a second branch of this action — it is
the existing `on_set_inst_filter("", "")` path (the filter sheet's
"All" commit), so this action has exactly one behaviour.

Why resolve the value in Rust (not host-passed): the trade-records page
runs on the ORPHAN interactor (`create()`, `session = Weak::new()`), so
the session-bound `MainTradeInteractor::get_current_inst_id()` is empty
there, and the legacy native `SelectBizManager.getCurrentBizInstrument()`
reads a *different* (stale) SP cache file when the Rust vs legacy gray
gates diverge — observed: panel on `ETH-USDT/MARGIN` (Rust
`core_trading_storage`) while the legacy `config.xml` still held
`LTC-USDT/SPOT`, so the seed filtered to the wrong pair. `TradeBizCache`
keeps the current-instrument identity single-sourced in Rust regardless
of Activity / session.

doc:
R5 — composite-seed projection for the V1 `StopProfitBean` the Kotlin
Fragment hands to `UniSetTpSlView.refreshTpslView(...)`.

# Why this lives Rust-side
The V1 path builds `StopProfitBean` directly in the confirm Fragment from
`OrderConfirmData` — a `unify_trade.biz.OrderConfirmData` dependency which
`pure/` Kotlin paths cannot import per R-MIG-021. V2 canonical pattern:
every field the bean needs is owned by this Rust state, projected through
`state()` as a structured uniffi::Record, and read by the pure Fragment to
construct the bean from a single snapshot reference (no field-by-field
Bundle plumbing on the Kotlin side, no `unify_trade.*` import).

# Field semantics
Mirrors V1 [`StopProfitBean`] field names verbatim so the Kotlin
translation is mechanical. `is_market_or_bbo` is derived from
`open_px.is_empty()` (V1 parity: empty `openPx` always means
market-or-BBO entry in the limit panel).

# Critical for input-enable
`open_px` MUST be non-empty for the composite's trigger ↔ percent
cross-input math to fire (R2.5 SEV-1 root cause when this field was
empty — V1 `UniSetTpSlView.refreshInputView()` short-circuits the
input enable + cross-input listener installation otherwise). The host
adapter must pass `state.price` from the parent panel; if the user
opens the sheet before typing a price, the composite falls back to the
live ticker subscription installed by `refreshTpslView` (V1 parity:
`ByPriceSpPresent.getChosePrice` falls back to `mView.getSelectMarketPx`
when `mBaseData.openPx.isEmpty() && from == FROM_ORDER`).

doc:
Date format enum that maps to native OKDateEnum.

Dates need to be localized on the native side because:

```kotlin

NONE(""),

}
```
